regions.summary: Guangshui (69%) and the Dawu county seat area (30%), on the Beijing-Guangzhou rail corridor at the Henan border.

candidates.name: Guangshui
candidates.meaning: "Wide water": county-level city, formed in 1988 from Yingshan county and named for the new rail town of Guangshui.
candidates.fit: Region holds 98% of the city and the city is 69% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

candidates.name: Wushengguan
candidates.meaning: "Martial victory pass": one of the Nine Passes of the Dabie range, on the Hubei-Henan border; also a Guangshui township.
candidates.fit: Pass lies in the region's north-east corner (Wushengguan township, 5% of people); the gateway to Xinyang across the border.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 30 hits with 湖北, most about Guangshui and the Jing-Han railway.
candidates.source_note: 京广铁路经市境东部武胜关、广办、杨寨，设广水站

candidates.name: Dawu
candidates.meaning: "Great awakening" (Buddhist enlightenment): county named in 1932 after the local Dawu mountain area.
candidates.fit: Holds only 52% of the county and is 30% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

regions.notes: Guangshui is the large county here. Yingshan (应山, the old county seat name) is skipped because Yingshan (英山) is a different county in region 7 and the spelling is identical.

regions.summary: Suizhou city (Cengdou district, 66%) and Sui county (29%).

candidates.name: Suizhou
candidates.meaning: Zhou-era Sui state, later Suizhou prefecture (907-1911); the city is the legendary birthplace of Yan Di.
candidates.fit: Seat of Suizhou/Suixian for over 1,500 years sits at the heart of this region; Cengdou district is 66% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city.

candidates.name: Cengdou
candidates.meaning: Named for the Zeng (Zeng/Sui) state, whose capital Cengdou lay here; Marquis Yi of Zeng's tomb is in the city.
candidates.fit: District is 66% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current district, so only moderately known.

regions.notes: Suizhou city proper is probably under 1M urban, so the city rule is not strictly needed, but the name still suits the centre.

regions.summary: Hong'an county (42%), the north of Wuhan's Huangpi district (38%), south-west Dawu (20%).

candidates.name: Hong'an
candidates.meaning: "Red peace": renamed from Huang'an in 1952 for the Red Army base and its many generals.
candidates.fit: Region holds 83% of the county, the largest unit at 42% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, well known as a revolutionary base.

candidates.name: Huang'an
candidates.meaning: "Yellow peace": the county's name from 1563 until 1952, named after Huangzhou and Anlu parts it was cut from.
candidates.fit: Same territory as Hong'an county, so it fits as the older name for the region's largest unit.
candidates.recognisability: Part of the Hong'an article; same place, so no gain in recognition over Hong'an.
candidates.source_note: 黄安县 (县, 1563-1911) 今湖北红安县

regions.notes: Huangpi's Mulan mountain (Mulan, as in Hua Mulan) lies on the Wuhan side; I left it to the Wuhan agent.

regions.summary: Anlu (52%) and Xiaochang (43%), north of Xiaogan city.

candidates.name: Anlu
candidates.meaning: "Peaceful land" (Anlu county since 394 CE); Anzhou and later the seat of De'an prefecture.
candidates.fit: Region holds 93% of the city, 52% of people; Anlu was the seat of the prefecture that covered the whole area.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city, famous as Li Bai's home for ten years.

candidates.name: De'an
candidates.meaning: "Virtue and peace": De'an prefecture (1119-1911) seated at Anlu.
candidates.fit: Prefecture covered today's Anlu, Guangshui, Yingcheng, Yunmeng and Xiaogan, so it also spans neighbouring regions 1, 6 and 8.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 135 hits with 湖北, but Dean (De'an county in Jiangxi) shares the spelling.
candidates.source_note: 辖区约今湖北省安陆、广水、应城、云梦、孝感等市县地

candidates.name: Xiaochang
candidates.meaning: "Filial prosperity": county name from 1932, echoing the Xiaogan 'filial piety' legend.
candidates.fit: Region holds 96% of the county, 43% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, little known.

regions.summary: Macheng city (75%) with the Xinzhou (Wuhan) strip and part of Hong'an.

candidates.name: Macheng
candidates.meaning: Named for the Ma Mountain (Ma Gu) and the old county town; Macheng county since 598 CE.
candidates.fit: Region holds 90% of the city; Macheng is 75% of people and 83% of area.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city, known for the Huguang-to-Sichuan migration and Dabie Mountains.

regions.notes: One obvious name; nothing better to add.

regions.summary: Xiaonan district, the centre of Xiaogan city (98%).

candidates.name: Xiaogan
candidates.meaning: "Filial feeling": named for the Han-era filial son Dong Yong, whose piety is said to have moved heaven.
candidates.fit: Holds the old centre of Xiaogan city (Xiaogan county seat 1129-1911) and 98% of Xiaonan district.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city, well known.

regions.notes: Faint region, 951 px; the city rule gives it the city's name.

regions.summary: Luotian (47%), Yingshan (32%) and bits of Xishui and Macheng: the southern slope of the Dabie Mountains.

candidates.name: Dabie
candidates.meaning: The Dabie Mountains ("great separate"), the watershed between the Yangtze and the Huai.
candidates.fit: Region is the southern slope in Hubei; Luotian and Yingshan counties are the Dabie core, with Tiantangzhai on the Anhui border. Neighbours across the border are already Jinzhai and Tianzhushan.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 774 hits with 湖北.
candidates.source_note: 河和长江的分水岭。主峰白马尖...天堂寨

candidates.name: Luotian
candidates.meaning: "Luo fields": county since 502 CE, named after the Luo surname families.
candidates.fit: Holds 100% of the county, 47% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

candidates.name: Yingshan
candidates.meaning: "Eagle mountain": named after Yingshan hill, county since 1267.
candidates.fit: Holds 100% of the county, 32% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

regions.notes: Dabie is a whole range but, per the landscape rule, fits this southern-slope region. Luotian is the safe county choice.

regions.summary: Yingcheng (48%), Yunmeng (37%), a slice of Hanchuan (14%).

candidates.name: Yunmeng
candidates.meaning: "Cloud dream": named for the ancient Yunmeng Marsh of Chu; the Shuihudi Qin bamboo slips were found here.
candidates.fit: Region holds 91% of the county, 37% of people; county has been Yunmeng since 546.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, famous for Qin bamboo slips and the old Yunmeng marsh.

candidates.name: Yingcheng
candidates.meaning: "City of the Ying": Ying county since 454 CE, known for gypsum and salt.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of the city, the largest unit at 48% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

regions.summary: Xishui (65%) and Tuanfeng (24%) on the Yangtze north bank east of Wuhan.

candidates.name: Xishui
candidates.meaning: Named for the Xi River, which runs through the county to the Yangtze.
candidates.fit: Region holds 85% of the county, which is 65% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, birthplace of Wen Yiduo.

candidates.name: Qishui
candidates.meaning: Old county name (502-1933) for the same place, from the Qi River; renamed Xishui in 1933.
candidates.fit: Same territory as Xishui county, seat 30 li east of today's town.
candidates.recognisability: Redirects to Xishui; 52 hits with 湖北, mostly about Xishui people ('湖北蕲水人').
candidates.source_note: 蕲水县 (县, 502-1911) 今湖北浠水县东三十里

candidates.name: Tuanfeng
candidates.meaning: "Group wind": county created 1995 around the town on the Yangtze.
candidates.fit: Only 24% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Small current county.

regions.notes: Qishui and Qichun (region 11) would read alike; Qishui is rated low for that reason.

regions.summary: Hanchuan (71%) and eastern Tianmen (27%) on the Han River's lower reach.

candidates.name: Hanchuan
candidates.meaning: "Han river plain": county named for the Han River, which runs through it before meeting the Yangtze.
candidates.fit: Holds only 50% of the city but it is 71% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

candidates.name: Chenhu
candidates.meaning: "Sunken lake": Chenhu wetland, a Ramsar site split by Hanchuan, Tianmen and Wuhan's Caidian.
candidates.fit: Chenhu town is 8% of the region's people; the lake lies in its heart.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article (沉湖湿地), 57 hits with 湖北, many just township lists.

regions.notes: The Tianmen share may be claimed by the central Hubei agent.

regions.summary: Qichun (75%) and Wuxue (24%) on the Yangtze north bank.

candidates.name: Qichun
candidates.meaning: "Qi spring": county since 202 BC, named for the Qi River; home of Li Shizhen, author of the Compendium of Materia Medica.
candidates.fit: Region holds 98% of the county, 75% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.

candidates.name: Qizhou
candidates.meaning: Prefecture and later route/fu, 583-1911, seated at today's Qizhou town in Qichun.
candidates.fit: In the Ming it governed Guangji (now Wuxue) and Huangmei, so it covers this region and region 13; Qizhou town is 5.5% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 112 hits with 湖北, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 蕲州仅代辖广济、黄梅两县

candidates.name: Wuxue
candidates.meaning: "Martial cave": the city's name from 1987, formerly Guangji county.
candidates.fit: Holds only 36% of the city, 24% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

regions.summary: Huangshi urban core (Huangshigang, Xialu, Xisaishan, Tieshan) plus Echeng district of Ezhou.

candidates.name: Huangshi
candidates.meaning: "Yellow stone": named for Huangshi Mountain/Port on the Yangtze; an iron and copper industrial city.
candidates.fit: Holds the old centre (Huangshigang) and most of Huangshi's urban districts, the city has 2.47M people.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city over 1M.

candidates.name: Xisaishan
candidates.meaning: Hill on the Yangtze south bank, subject of Liu Yuxi's poem 'Xisaishan huaigu' and Zhang Zhihe's 'white egrets'.
candidates.fit: Xisaishan district is 17% of people; mountain stands on the Huangshi riverfront.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 17 hits with 湖北, but also a current district name.
candidates.source_note: 西塞山位于湖北省黄石市西塞山区东部，坐长江南岸

regions.notes: Huangshi's rest (Daye) is another region, which can take Daye. Echeng (Ezhou) is 35% here; Ezhou's own region may be named separately.

regions.summary: Huangmei county (83%) with Susong (Anhui, 15%) at the Jiangxi-Anhui-Hubei corner.

candidates.name: Huangmei
candidates.meaning: "Yellow plum": county since 598 CE; home of Huangmei opera and the Fourth and Fifth Patriarch temples of Chan Buddhism.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of the county, 83% of people.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, famous for Huangmei opera.

candidates.name: Longgan
candidates.meaning: "Dragon-moved lake": freshwater lake on the Hubei-Anhui border, shared by Huangmei and Susong.
candidates.fit: Lake lies on the Huangmei-Susong line, which is the seam of this region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 179 hits with 湖北, though many are about its farm and offices.
candidates.source_note: 湖北省和安徽省交界处...黄梅县和宿松县共有

regions.notes: Region crosses into Anhui (Susong), so a province-neutral name like Longgan is worth considering, though Huangmei is the stronger name.
The Tongshan label sits in this region; Tongshan county is only 34% of it, so the name may fit Chongyang better in places. Anita chose it, so leave it.
